info.title: Picciuli API
info.description:
REST API of [Picciuli](https://github.com/antoniobarba/picciuli), a personal
budgeting and money tracking engine.

Every user owns a private book: accounts, categories, transactions, periods,
budgets, securities and settings are never shared between users.

**Authentication.** Send an OpenID Connect access token (JWT) from the identity
provider in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

**Conventions.** Amounts are integers in minor units (cents) and signed from
your point of view (positive = money coming to you). Quantities, prices and
exchange rates are decimal strings. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; ranges are
inclusive. `PATCH` bodies only change the fields they contain.

**Errors** always have the shape `{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<message>"}`.

post.description:
Load the data of a Picciuli database file (SQLite) into your book.

With `mode=merge`, accounts, categories, securities and periods with the
same name (or ISIN, or days) are reused, and transactions identical to
existing ones are skipped, so importing a file twice adds nothing.
Merging requires the same currency and decimal digits. With
`mode=replace`, all your data is deleted first and the file's settings
are adopted. Either way the import is all-or-nothing.

The file must use the current schema version (open older files once with
an up-to-date Picciuli library) and its data must respect the same
rules as data entered by hand, otherwise the request fails with 422.
Only one import per user runs at a time (409 otherwise).

CostMethod.title: CostMethod
CostMethod.description:
How the cost of sold shares is computed when a sale is recorded.

The cost removed from the account sets the realized gain of the sale:
`gain = proceeds - cost`.
